body:
From the pre-release security review of the server's network interface
(2026-07-26). Post-1.8.1.

## Problem

routes/lists.py:36 deliberately returns a uniform 403 so a non-member "can't
distinguish 'not found' from 'not yours' (no existence-leak)". /sync breaks that
property for the same information. Measured, as an account that is a member of
nothing:

    item push naming a nonexistent list  -> 422 unknown_list
    item push naming an existing list    -> 403 not_a_member

sync.py:561 checks _list_exists() before the membership check, so the two cases
are distinguishable.

Severity is low while list ids are client-generated UUIDs. It is worth fixing
anyway because ids are attacker-CHOOSABLE (see the invite-delimiter ticket:
_apply_list accepts any string as an id), so an attacker can create memorable or
guessable ids and this oracle then confirms which ones exist.

## Fix

Return 403 not_a_member for both cases in _apply_item — i.e. do the membership
check first, or collapse the unknown-list case into the same error.

Check before changing: unknown_list is a documented wire-contract error code
(docs/wire-contract.md) and the Android quarantine flow (T-32) may branch on it.
If a client treats unknown_list as "drop this row permanently" but not_a_member
as "retry later", collapsing them changes client behaviour for a genuinely
unknown list. Confirm both clients' handling before merging, and update
docs/wire-contract.md either way.

## Verification

Test that a non-member gets an identical status and body for a nonexistent list
id and for an existing-but-foreign list id.
title: sync: list-existence oracle (422 unknown_list vs 403 not_a_member) defeats the uniform-403 rule
